name: Toolbar
description: A container grouping controls (buttons, menubuttons, checkboxes) that reduces tab stops by treating the toolbar as a single tab stop with arrow key navigation.

keyboard_interactions.action: Moves focus into toolbar on first or previously focused control
Moves focus out of the toolbar
Moves focus to previous control (horizontal); optionally wraps
Moves focus to next control (horizontal); optionally wraps

optional_attributes.description: vertical for vertical; default is horizontal

notes: role='toolbar' exists to make a long row of buttons ONE Tab stop instead of twenty. If you have three buttons, you do not need it — plain buttons are better.
Roving tabindex is mandatory: tabindex='0' on exactly one control, '-1' on the rest. Without it the role is a lie — it claims to be one stop and is not.
Real focus moves here (call .focus()). Do not use aria-activedescendant.
Name the toolbar (aria-label='Text formatting'). Several unnamed toolbars are indistinguishable.
Do not nest interactive controls that need their own arrow keys (a listbox, a combobox) directly in a toolbar — the arrow handling collides. Wrap them, or reconsider.
aria-orientation='vertical' if the toolbar is vertical, so Up/Down are the expected keys instead of Left/Right.
A toolbar containing only links is just navigation — use <nav>.
native_element: none — but a plain group of <button>s with no toolbar role is often better

raweb_criteria.reason: The toolbar role and its accessible name must be exposed.
Arrow keys must move between controls; every control stays operable by pointer.
The focused control must be visibly indicated as focus roves.
Roving tabindex makes the toolbar a single, coherent Tab stop.
Tab must always leave the toolbar — the classic roving-tabindex trap.
